title: Gingerbread Muffins with Crystallised Ginger
changes_from_base: A dark brown sugar, treacle and buttermilk batter spiced with ginger, cinnamon and allspice, with crystallised ginger instead of fruit; no topping sugar.
summary: Dark, moist muffins spiced with ginger, cinnamon and allspice, with treacle and chewy crystallised ginger.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and grease the holes of the tin with butter or oil.

steps.title: Spice
steps.text: Whisk the flour, bicarbonate of soda, salt, ground ginger, cinnamon and allspice together in a medium bowl until the spices are evenly spread.

steps.title: Wet
steps.text: In a bigger bowl whisk the eggs, dark brown sugar, treacle and buttermilk until smooth. Pour in the melted butter and whisk hard until the mix turns thick and glossy.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk in half the spiced flour until it starts to come together. Add the rest with two-thirds of the chopped crystallised ginger and stir with a spatula only until no flour shows.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scoop the batter into the tin and scatter over the remaining ginger. Bake 18-22 min, turning the tin once, until a cocktail stick in the middle comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 5 min in the tin, then move to the rack; they are good slightly warm.

tips: The most common mistake is beating after the flour goes in; stir just until combined so the muffins stay soft.
Weigh treacle on a lightly oiled spoon so it slides off.
Dust crystallised ginger in a little of the flour if the pieces stick together.
storage: Keep in an airtight box for up to 3 days; they get stickier and more gingery by day two. Freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
